text:
carly-seller: Hey team — Greenline POC kickoff. They want a Redwood Private deployment in their AWS account behind their Transit VPC (TGW) talking to a spoke VPC. Key asks: preserve client source IP to backend, SNI passthrough so their TLS routing works, short failover to hosted API, and a minimal firewall/runbook + EIP guidance. Also they dropped a SOC2 security questionnaire (link below). Can infra/eng confirm blockers and what we need from the customer?

sam-net: Short answer: doable but depends on connectivity choice. VPC peering (or TGW routes without NAT) will preserve client src IP. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) will terminate at ENIs and flows will appear from the endpoint ENI — that usually means you can't see original client IPs unless you pass it in an application header. If they need src IP for ACLing or app logs, prefer peering/TGW routing w/o NAT.

sam-net: SNI: as long as we do TCP passthrough and don't terminate TLS in our proxy, SNI is preserved. If the customer inserts a TLS-inspecting proxy (man-in-the-middle), SNI could be stripped. For mTLS we need cert exchange and a key plan.

maya-se: Pricing note: for the POC we can cover up to 2 EIPs + one small NAT gateway for testing. Production EIP/NAT costs are billed to the customer. Dedicated Private deployment license/commit affects infra add-on pricing; I’ll attach the quick pricing sheet after this thread. Also ask the customer to reserve a /28 subnet for our ENIs if using PrivateLink (we prefer that to avoid IP exhaustion). :eyes:

nate-security: SOC2/security checklist items we need from Greenline: KMS key lifecycle and ownership detail, VPC Flow Logs to S3/CloudWatch (retention window), IAM roles we will assume (least-privilege policy), and confirmation that no TLS termination happens in front of the service unless documented. Please upload the filled questionnaire; I flagged the sections on key management and logging.

liu-ops: Runbook + firewall snippet for their network team (drop-in):

Allowlist (peering/TGW option):
- Allow TCP 443 from customer spoke CIDRs -> service subnets (no NAT).
- Allow TCP 15001 (health) and 15002 (admin) from ops CIDR (temporary during POC).
- Ensure route table in spoke points to TGW for service subnets.

Allowlist (PrivateLink option):
- Create Interface Endpoint ENIs in their subnets; security group inbound from spoke CIDRs: TCP 443.
- Route tables don't need peering but must allow traffic to ENI IPs.

Example security group rule (copy/paste):
```
Type: Custom TCP
Protocol: TCP
PortRange: 443
Source: 10.10.0.0/16  # customer's spoke CIDR
Description: Allow app traffic to Redwood interface endpoint ENIs
```
Also enable VPC Flow Logs and send to S3 for the audit window.

liu-ops: Note about source IP preservation: if they put a NAT gateway or an egress proxy in front of the traffic, the client IP will be lost. If they need original IP in headers, we can add an X-Forwarded-For header but that requires TLS termination at the proxy layer.

jon-deploybot: POC ticket created: RL-4591 — assigned to @sam-net. Checklist item: collect reserved /28 (if PrivateLink) or confirm TGW routes + route table snapshots. ETA: 3 business days to produce a full handoff doc.

rita-sales: Customer asked if we can meet RTO < 2 minutes for failover. Is that realistic with TGW + Route53 health checks? :thinking_face:

sam-net: Short: Yes with active/standby across two AZs or regions + Route53 weighted failover + health checks, we can aim for <2m. Needs testing in their network (some proxies take longer). Cross-region peering has costs and slight complexity with TGW attachments — mention that in the pricing pack.

carly-seller: Thanks all. Greenline uploaded the questionnaire: https://s3.amazonaws.com/greenline/poc/soc2-q.pdf. I'll schedule an SRE call Fri 10am PST. Action items: @maya-se send pricing sheet, @sam-net produce connectivity checklist, @nate-security review questionnaire, @liu-ops produce final SG/NACL snippet. :thumbsup:
